title: Swarm Robot State Machine
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Interactive Mermaid state machine for a swarm robot with SEARCH, FOLLOW, DANCE, and AVOID states. Event buttons step the robot through transitions (or show that a state ignores an event), dashed arrows show that AVOID can interrupt any state, and a quiz asks students to classify robot situations by state.

educational.topic: State machine pattern for multi-behavior robots
learningObjectives: Explain how a state machine organizes a robot's competing behaviors into named states and transitions.
Classify robot situations into the SEARCH, FOLLOW, DANCE, or AVOID state.
Trace the state changes produced by a sequence of events, including events a state ignores.
Explain why the AVOID transition must be reachable from every other state.
standards: CSTA 3A-AP-15: Justify the selection of specific control structures when tradeoffs involve implementation, readability, and program performance.

controls.label: Explore events
controls.purpose: Send events and watch the current state follow the arrows (default).

controls.label: Classify quiz
controls.purpose: Read a robot situation and click the matching state.

controls.label: Restart
controls.purpose: Return the robot to SEARCH and restart the quiz.

controls.label: Event buttons
controls.purpose: leader signal found, signal lost, dance beat received, routine finished, obstacle too close, path clear.

userInterface.hoverTargets: Every state box and every transition arrow or label shows a plain-language explanation on hover or click.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through worked example followed by a classification quiz
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Event-driven step-through with highlighted current state and fired transition, plus click-to-classify quiz with feedback
keyQuestions: What happens when a state receives an event it has no arrow for?
Why does every state have an arrow to AVOID?
Which state is the robot in when it has just lost the leader's signal?
commonMisconceptions: The robot runs all four behaviors in order every loop (only the current state's code runs).
Every event changes the state (a state ignores events it has no transition for).
AVOID is just another step in the routine (it is a safety interrupt reachable from every state).
assessmentOpportunities: Trace the state path for a given list of events.
Exit ticket: design the arrows for a new CHARGE state.
